tweet_summary: The official @WhiteHouse account (4.7M followers) posts a Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas meme edit ('Ah shit, here we go again' CJ meme + thermal blast footage + GTA V 'wasted' screen) captioned 'OPERATION EPIC FURY • Destroy Iran's missile arsenal. • Destroy their navy. • Ensure they NEVER get a nuclear weapon.' 17.9M impressions — a massive viral propaganda post mocking war coverage with Gen Z gaming memes.
why_note_decision: The video is an obvious GTA-meme edit posted by the official White House account itself. No one was deceived — top comments are all reactions to the WH using GTA imagery for war propaganda ('using clips from Grand Theft Auto in pro-war propaganda', 'OPERATION EPSTEIN'S FURY', 'gen z bait videos'). The meme nature is the POINT of the post. The original note explains 'the video is edited footage from GTA: San Andreas, not real military footage. Operation Epic Fury is an actual U.S. operation against Iranian targets' — which is correct but completely unnecessary; nobody thought the CJ-character animation was real footage. Community overwhelmingly rejected (113 noteNotNeeded, 104 missingKeyPoints, 51 incorrect on 233 ratings).
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The post is from the official @WhiteHouse account itself and uses unmistakable GTA: San Andreas imagery (CJ meme, 'Ah shit, here we go again', GTA V 'wasted' screen) — no one is deceived about the video's source. Top comments universally treat it as a propaganda meme, not real footage. FAIL any note that (a) repeats the original failure of solemnly explaining 'this is GTA, not real footage' on overtly-meme content from the official source account, (b) writes a missing-key-points note about the operation being real — that ISN'T the meaningful claim; the meaningful 'claim' is the political posture, which is opinion/framing. The pipeline must not lecture viewers about famous meme imagery posted by the originator with intent.

Operation Epic Fury referenced in CENTCOM and Fox News (real US Iran-strike operation)
fact_check.notes: Video is unmistakably GTA imagery (CJ, 'wasted' screen, the iconic 'Ah shit, here we go again' meme). Posted by the official @WhiteHouse account as deliberate Gen Z meme propaganda. The 'note explains the meme' framing is the textbook false positive.

importance.lens_rationale: 17.9M impressions on a White House propaganda post mixing memes with real war messaging. Important false-positive case — pipeline must not over-correct overt propaganda memes; the more important question (was the strike justified/effective) is framing, not fact-checkable here.
